note: Standardised delay reason codes. Consistent use across all sites and departments is critical — a reason code used differently by different supervisors produces meaningless Pareto analysis. The Description field tells supervisors exactly when to use each code.

items.Title: Wet weather — rainfall
items.Description: Use when active rainfall or waterlogged conditions directly prevented work from commencing or continuing. Not to be used for residual wet conditions after rain has stopped — use 'Wet conditions — post rain' instead.

items.Title: Wet conditions — post rain
items.Description: Use when ground conditions following a previous rain event prevented work. Area was too wet or muddy to safely operate. Rain had stopped but conditions had not recovered.

items.Title: High winds
items.Description: Use when wind speed exceeded safe operating limits for the work type (e.g. blasting, crane lifts, float operations). Document actual wind speed if recorded.

items.Title: Road inaccessible — weather
items.Description: Use when access to the work area was blocked by weather-damaged roads, flooding, or wet crossings. Equipment and personnel could not safely reach the work site.

items.Title: Road inaccessible — not yet constructed
items.Description: Use when access road had not been completed before this task was scheduled to start. A preceding road works or earthworks task was not complete. This is a CONTROLLABLE delay — indicates a planning sequencing error.

items.Title: Area not cleared — blast pending
items.Description: Use when access to the work area was blocked because a blast exclusion zone was active or a blast had not yet been fired. Post Blast works not yet complete.

items.Title: Area flooded — dewatering incomplete
items.Description: Use when the target work area was flooded and dewatering had not been completed before this task was scheduled to start. Indicates Dewater task was not complete in time.

items.Title: Equipment breakdown — own department
items.Description: Use when plant or equipment allocated to this task suffered a mechanical failure and could not operate. Equipment was owned by the responsible department.

items.Title: Equipment not available — shared resource
items.Description: Use when the required equipment was working elsewhere and could not be released in time. Equipment is a shared resource across departments (e.g. float, pump, dozer).

items.Title: Equipment not available — float delay
items.Description: Use specifically when the float (low-loader) was not available or was delayed, preventing equipment transport to the work location.

items.Title: Insufficient crew — absenteeism
items.Description: Use when there were not enough personnel to safely and productively perform the task due to unplanned absences (sick leave, LWOP, etc.).

items.Title: Insufficient crew — FIFO rotation
items.Description: Use when crew numbers were reduced due to FIFO changeover timing and replacements had not yet arrived on site.

items.Title: Crew redeployed — higher priority
items.Description: Use when the crew assigned to this task was redeployed to a different task by the superintendent or shift supervisor due to an emerging higher priority. The redeployment was a deliberate management decision.

items.Title: Preceding task not complete
items.Description: Use when this task could not start because a predecessor task had not been completed. The task sequence was correct but the predecessor ran longer than planned. Identify the specific predecessor task in the notes.

items.Title: Waiting on permit or approval
items.Description: Use when work was delayed because a required permit, design approval, inspection, or regulatory approval had not been obtained before the task was due to start. Examples: blast permit, environmental approval, electrical isolation permit.

items.Title: Scope change — design revision
items.Description: Use when the scope of the enabling task changed after it was scheduled — design updated by Survey or Engineering, requiring rework or additional work beyond original scope.

items.Title: Scope change — field conditions
items.Description: Use when field conditions discovered during execution (e.g. unexpected ground conditions, buried services, unstable material) required more work than planned.

items.Title: Safety stop — hazard identified
items.Description: Use when work was stopped to manage a safety hazard that was identified during execution. Includes falling ground, unstable benches, unplanned water inflows, or any hazard requiring work cessation.

items.Title: Safety stop — exclusion zone
items.Description: Use when work could not proceed because another activity created an exclusion zone over the work area (blasting, crane lift, etc.) that was not planned.

items.Title: Material not available — gravel/reject
items.Description: Use when road works or earthworks were delayed because sheeting material (gravel or reject) was not available at the required time. Indicates materials coordination failure.

items.Title: Unplanned task displaced planned task
items.Description: Use when an unplanned enabling task arose during the shift that consumed the resources allocated to this planned task. The displacement was not a deliberate redeployment but an unplanned response.

items.Title: Other — see notes
items.Description: Use only when no other reason code accurately describes the delay. The notes field MUST be completed with a clear explanation. If this code is being used frequently, notify the mine planner — a new reason code may be needed.
